name: Bergerac

limits: For red wine, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec and Merlot together: at least 75%
For white wine, Muscadelle, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Sémillon together: at least 75%
For white wine, Chenin Blanc and Ondenc together: at most 20%
rules.yield_base: 67 hl/ha for white, 62 for rosé, 60 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

notes: Bergerac whites and reds are dry, and its rosés are dry or off-dry.
The reds are fruity, sometimes richly tannic, and a little austere when young.
The whites are floral and fruity with some acidity, and fuller Sémillon or Muscadelle wines gain complexity over a few years.

blurb.text: A South West France wine area around the town of Bergerac in the Dordogne, just east of Bordeaux. Rules allow Merlot, the Cabernets, Cot, Sémillon and Sauvignon.
